Worker pools

A worker pool bounds how many jobs run at the same time. Size it from measured resource use rather than from the length of the queue, because every live worker holds memory, file descriptors and a connection to the database.

Docs / Worker pools

Creating a pool

Call runtime.NewPool with the ceiling you measured. See the queue reference for how jobs arrive.

pool := runtime.NewPool(runtime.PoolConfig{
	Workers: 8,
	Queue:   jobs,
})
if err := pool.Start(ctx); err != nil {
	return fmt.Errorf("starting the pool: %w", err)
}
defer pool.Drain()

Choosing the ceiling

  • Start at the number of cores and measure.
  • Raise it while latency is flat and the queue is not empty.
  • Stop when memory per worker times the ceiling reaches half of what the host has.
SettingDefaultMeaning
Workers4jobs running at the same time
Backlog1024jobs held before Submit blocks
Draining is not cancellation: a drained pool finishes the jobs it already accepted.
